type.title: Which type fits?
type.body: If your code runs on a server, choose “Web application” – it receives a client secret. Apps in the browser or on devices cannot protect a secret and secure the sign-in with PKCE instead.

configure.title: What is a redirect URI?
configure.body: After signing in, Aegis sends the browser back to this address of your application. It must be registered exactly – without wildcards. HTTP is only allowed for localhost.

credentials.title: Almost done
credentials.body: With the issuer, client ID and secret your application can sign users in. Choose who may sign in on the Access tab afterwards.

settings.protectionsDescription: These rules always apply and cannot be turned off.

protectionItems.roles: Roles are hierarchical: users only sign in to applications, admins also manage Aegis. Every request is checked against the permissions of its role on the server.
protectionItems.applicationAccess: Applications can be restricted to assigned accounts; revoking access ends sign-ins and tokens immediately.
protectionItems.pkce: PKCE with S256 only – required for public applications, set per application for confidential ones. A code_challenge that is sent is always verified.
protectionItems.redirectUris: Redirect URIs are matched exactly – no wildcards.
protectionItems.codeFlow: Authorization code flow only – no implicit or password grant.
protectionItems.argon2: Passwords stored as Argon2id hashes ({memory} MiB, {iterations} iterations, parallelism {parallelism}).
protectionItems.encryption: Signing keys and client secrets are encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
protectionItems.rateLimit: Sign-in attempts are limited per IP address.

settings.auditRetentionDescription: How long audit entries are kept ({min}–{max} days). Older entries are removed automatically.
